newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Seagate agrees 148 mln punt Irish investment.
newsitem.headline: Seagate agrees 148 mln punt Irish investment.

text.p: Seagate Technology has agreed a 148 million Irish pound ($224 million) investment in southern Ireland, minister for Enterprise and Employment Richard Bruton said on Thursday.

Seagate, supported by state-owned inward investment body, IDA Ireland, will establish a manufacturing facility in Ringaskiddy, County Cork, creating more than 1,000 jobs within the next three years, Bruton said.

"This is the largest ever IDA supported manufacturing announcement for Cork," Bruton said. "It is especially significant that Seagate Technology, the world's largest producer of hard disc drives for the computer industry, has chosen Cork for its second major investment in the Republic."

Seagate has 46 sales offices and 20 manufacturing facilities world-wide. It employs more than 108,000 people and recorded net profits of 400 million Irish pounds on sales of 4.4 billion punts in the last nine months.
The multinational group set up a facility in Ireland initially in 1995. It currently employs 1,500 people in its midland site in Clonmel, County Tipperary.
Last Friday, it announced it was building a second factory in Londonderry in Northern Ireland, creating 1,000 jobs in addition to the 1,125 employed in its existing plant there.
